hero.description: Estadio Azteca is the only stadium to have hosted two World Cup Finals (1970 and 1986). In 2026, it opens the entire tournament — making Mexico City the epicenter of the world's biggest sporting event for the third time. There's nowhere on Earth with deeper football history.

stadium.name: Estadio Azteca
stadium.address: Calz. de Tlalpan 3465, Santa Úrsula Coapa, Coyoacán, 04650 CDMX, México
stadium.transport: Take Metro Line 2 to Tasqueña station, then Tren Ligero (light rail) Line 1 directly to Estadio Azteca station — about 45 minutes from the city center. Metrobús Line 4 also serves the stadium. Uber and DiDi are practical for mid-distance trips but traffic around the stadium on match day is severe.

quick_facts.matches_hosted: 5 matches — Group stage through Round of 16
quick_facts.altitude: 2,240 meters (7,349 feet) above sea level — acclimatize before exertion
quick_facts.fan_hub_status: Major fan hub expected at Zócalo; local watch parties throughout the city

weather.june: Warm and partly cloudy, highs around 22–24°C (72–75°F). The rainy season begins — afternoon thunderstorms are common.
weather.july: Similar to June. Afternoon storms, mild temperatures, very green city. Evenings are cool.
packing_tips: Bring a compact rain jacket or poncho — afternoon storms come fast and heavy
The city sits at 2,240m — altitude affects many visitors. Avoid alcohol until acclimatized
Light layers for the day; a warm layer for evening at altitude
Comfortable walking shoes with grip — streets can be slick after rain

airports.name: Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez
airports.distance_to_stadium: About 20 km from Azteca, 15 km from Polanco
transfer_options: Metro Line 5 from Terminal 1 Airport to Pantitlán, transfer to Line 1 or 3 toward center — cheap but crowded with luggage
Authorized airport taxis (pay at the booth before exit) — roughly $15–20 USD to Polanco or Condesa
Uber is available from Terminal 2 (official pickup zone). Terminal 1 Uber pickup is slightly complicated — follow airport signs
The Mexibús bus rapid transit also connects Terminal 2 to Indios Verdes
airports.notes: Use authorized airport taxis (pay at the counter inside the terminal) or Uber — avoid unofficial taxi touts. Terminal 1 (domestic) and Terminal 2 (international) are connected by a free shuttle.

airports.name: Aeropuerto Internacional Felipe Ángeles
airports.distance_to_stadium: About 55 km from Downtown Mexico City
transfer_options: Suburban train (Tren Suburbano) to Buenavista station in Downtown CDMX — about 45 minutes
Bus connections to the metro system available at Buenavista
airports.notes: New airport north of the city. Less crowded than MEX. If flying low-cost carriers, confirm which airport and factor in the longer transit time.

public_transit: Metro Line 2 to Tasqueña, then Tren Ligero Line 1 directly to Estadio Azteca — the classic route
Metrobús Line 4 serves Calzada de Tlalpan corridor
Expect extreme crowding on match days — allow 90 minutes for stadium transit
rideshare: Uber and DiDi are widely available and safe throughout CDMX
Traffic around the stadium hours before kickoff is severe — rideshare adds 30–60 min to estimated time
Post-match, walk several blocks away from the stadium before requesting a rideshare pickup
driving_parking: Parking around Azteca is available but the access roads are chaotic on match days
Driving is not recommended unless staying in Coyoacán or very close to the stadium
Hoy No Circula restrictions may apply to your rental depending on the last digit of the license plate — check before driving
walking_biking: The stadium area south of the city is not walkable from most tourist hotels
ECOBICI bike share does not extend to the stadium zone
match_day_tips: Arrive at least 2 hours early — Azteca holds 87,000+ and queues are long
Carry cash for food vendors and metro fares — cards not always accepted at smaller vendors
Stay hydrated — altitude makes exertion harder even in mild weather
Keep your phone charged and have your e-ticket downloaded offline before you leave the hotel

fan_hubs.name: Zócalo Fan Hub
fan_hubs.location: Plaza de la Constitución, Centro Histórico, CDMX
fan_hubs.description: One of the largest public plazas in the world, the Zócalo is expected to be the main fan hub for the 2026 tournament — giant screens, live music, street food from every region of Mexico, and tens of thousands of fans. The scale and energy here will be unlike any other host city.
transport_tips: Metro Line 2 to Zócalo/Tenochtitlan station — right at the plaza
Multiple bus and Metrobús routes serve the Centro Histórico

fan_hubs.name: Parque Lincoln Fan Hub
fan_hubs.description: Polanco's upscale neighbourhood park becomes a high-end fan zone area with rooftop bars overlooking the screens, restaurants from acclaimed chefs, and a more international crowd. An excellent option for fans staying in Polanco.
transport_tips: Short walk from major Polanco hotels

fan_hubs.name: Condesa / Roma Fan Streets
fan_hubs.location: Álvaro Obregón and Ámsterdam Ave, Condesa–Roma Norte
fan_hubs.description: The Condesa and Roma Norte neighbourhoods come alive on match days. Bars and restaurants spill onto tree-lined streets, speakers play cumbias and match commentary, and the vibe is unmistakably CDMX. This is where the local young crowd watches.
transport_tips: Metro Line 1 to Insurgentes or Sonora
Walkable between Roma Norte and Condesa

neighborhoods.name: Polanco
neighborhoods.best_for: Luxury hotels, fine dining, safety, international crowd
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safest area in CDMX for tourists. Well-patrolled, walkable, and with major hotel brands.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Metro Line 7 to Barranca del Muerto, transfer to Tren Ligero — about 60 min to Azteca
neighborhoods.description: The most upscale tourist neighbourhood. Luxury hotel brands, Michelin-class restaurants, and tree-lined boulevards. Excellent safety record and comfortable tourist infrastructure.

neighborhoods.name: Condesa
neighborhoods.best_for: Boutique hotels, café culture, soccer bars
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Very safe for tourists. Low-key residential feel with active street life.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Metro Line 1 to Insurgentes, then Line 2 to Tasqueña, then Tren Ligero — about 60–70 min
neighborhoods.description: Art deco architecture, tree-lined streets, and the best café and restaurant scene in CDMX. A huge favourite for international travellers. Watch party energy here is incredible.

neighborhoods.name: Roma Norte
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Generally safe for tourists, especially on main corridors. Use street sense at night.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Metro Line 1 to Sonora, then transfer to Line 2 to Tasqueña, then Tren Ligero — about 60 min
neighborhoods.description: Mexico City's hippest neighbourhood. Independent restaurants, mezcal bars, street art, and the most creative food scene in the city. Budget-friendly and walkable to Condesa.

neighborhoods.name: Centro Histórico
neighborhoods.best_for: History, budget options, proximity to Zócalo fan hub
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Busy during the day, use extra caution at night especially away from the main tourist corridor.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Metro Line 2 to Tasqueña, then Tren Ligero — about 50 min
neighborhoods.description: The ancient heart of the city with Aztec ruins, the Metropolitan Cathedral, and the iconic Zócalo. Walk distance to the expected main fan hub. Historic and atmospheric.

neighborhoods.name: Coyoacán
neighborhoods.best_for: Culture, bohemian atmosphere, proximity to stadium
neighborhoods.stadium_access: About 15–20 min to Azteca by rideshare or Tren Ligero
neighborhoods.description: A quiet, tree-shaded neighbourhood with a colonial central plaza, Frida Kahlo Museum, and Leon Trotsky Museum. Closest neighbourhood to Estadio Azteca for fans wanting easy match-day access.

hotels.name: Camino Real Polanco
hotels.best_for: Classic luxury, business amenities, large rooms

hotels.name: NH Collection Mexico City Centro Histórico

booking_links.label: Browse all Mexico City hotels on Booking.com →

bars.name: Cantina La No. 20
bars.notes: Beloved traditional cantina. Classic CDMX atmosphere — botanas (free snacks) with every drink order.

bars.name: Jules Basement
bars.notes: American-style sports bar in Polanco. Reliable screens and a mixed local/expat crowd.

bars.name: Salón Ríos
bars.notes: A classic CDMX canteen with match energy and cheap beers. Authentic experience.

bars.name: La Glorieta
bars.notes: Outdoor terrace on Ámsterdam's traffic-free ring. Beautiful for afternoon matches.

bars.name: Biergarten Condesa
bars.notes: Beer garden popular with Mexico national team supporters. Big screens on major match days.

transport.summary: Mexico City has one of the world's largest metro systems — 195 stations, 5 MXN per ride, and good coverage. For the tournament, combine Metro with Tren Ligero for Azteca, and use Uber/DiDi for everything else.
tips: Metro fare is 5 MXN per ride — get a rechargeable card at any station kiosk
Line 2 + Tren Ligero is the classic Azteca route from downtown — allow 60–90 min on match days
Avoid metro during weekday rush hours (7–9am, 6–8pm) — it's extremely crowded
Uber and DiDi are safe, reliable, and very affordable — preferred for evening travel
Metrobús (BRT) is faster than regular buses on major avenues like Insurgentes
ECOBICI bike share works well in Condesa, Roma Norte, and Polanco

fan_zones.name: Zócalo Fan Hub
fan_zones.location: Plaza de la Constitución, Centro Histórico
fan_zones.description: One of the world's largest public plazas, expected to host a massive fan hub with giant screens, live music, and street food throughout the tournament.

fan_zones.name: Parque Lincoln Fan Hub
fan_zones.description: Polanco's upscale park fan zone with nearby rooftop bars and high-end food options.

soccer_culture.community_notes: Mexico City is one of the most football-obsessed cities on Earth. The Azteca holds 87,000 and regularly fills for Liga MX fixtures. Club América and Cruz Azul both call the city home. The passion here on match days needs to be experienced.
local_clubs: Atlas (Liga MX — technically Guadalajara but CDMX fans follow)
historic_venues: Estadio Azteca (1970 and 1986 World Cup Final)

tourist_hits.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
tourist_hits.notes: World-class museum of Mesoamerican history in Chapultepec Park. Give it half a day minimum.

tourist_hits.name: Teotihuacan Pyramids
tourist_hits.notes: Day trip 50 km from the city. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun for views across the ancient city. Go early.

tourist_hits.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul)
tourist_hits.notes: In Coyoacán neighbourhood. Book tickets in advance — sells out weeks ahead.

tourist_hits.name: Zócalo and Metropolitan Cathedral
tourist_hits.notes: The heart of the city. The cathedral and Templo Mayor ruins are free to visit.

tourist_hits.name: Chapultepec Park
tourist_hits.notes: Massive urban park with a castle, multiple museums, and the best strolling in the city.

local_favorites.name: Mercado de Jamaica (flower market)
local_favorites.notes: Early morning flower market — extraordinary visual experience and incredibly cheap.

local_favorites.name: Lucha libre at Arena México
local_favorites.notes: Tuesdays and Fridays. Colourful, theatrical, loud, and unforgettable.

local_favorites.name: Tepito flea market
local_favorites.notes: The real CDMX — go with a local if possible. Cash only, leave valuables at the hotel.

local_favorites.name: Xochimilco canal boats (trajineras)
local_favorites.notes: Float through ancient canals in colourful boats with mariachi and food vendors. Very local.

areas: Roma Norte / Condesa — best concentration of international and elevated Mexican restaurants
Polanco — fine dining and cocktail bars, including multiple top-50 world restaurants
Coyoacán — traditional taquerias and mezcal bars around the main square
Centro Histórico — traditional cantinas and market food stalls

recommendations.name: El Hidalguense
recommendations.notes: Slow-cooked barbacoa in Roma — widely considered the best taco in the city. Cash only. Saturday and Sunday only.

recommendations.name: Contramar
recommendations.notes: Legendary seafood restaurant in Roma Norte. Book weeks ahead. The tuna tostadas are world-famous.

recommendations.name: Quintonil
recommendations.notes: One of the best restaurants in Latin America. Modern Mexican cuisine with an extraordinary tasting menu.

local_resources.emergency_info: Emergency: 911. Non-emergency CDMX police: (55) 5208-9898. Hospital: Hospital Ángeles Polanco, (55) 5229-8999.

walk_bike.walkability_summary: Condesa, Roma Norte, and Polanco are excellent for walking — tree-shaded, flat, and vibrant. Ámsterdam Avenue in Condesa is a pedestrianized oval popular with joggers and cyclists.
walk_bike.bikeability_summary: ECOBICI bike share covers Condesa, Roma, Polanco, and the Centro with about 7,000 bikes at 480 stations.
walk_bike.bike_share_notes: ECOBICI day passes available in the ECOBICI app. First 45 minutes of each ride is free with a pass.

pickup_soccer.name: Parque España
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Small futsal courts with informal games throughout the day. Local neighbourhood regulars, very welcoming.
pickup_soccer.schedule_notes: Active most evenings and weekend mornings.

pickup_soccer.name: CU (Ciudad Universitaria) Fields
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Multiple grass fields around the UNAM campus. Some organized pickup and open access fields.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Teotihuacan Pyramids
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Must-do day trip. Take an early bus from Autobuses del Norte terminal or book a guided tour. Bring water, hat, and sunscreen. Go before 10am.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Desierto de los Leones
outdoors_day_trips.distance: About 20 km southwest of the city center
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Quiet pine forest with hiking trails and a historic Carmelite convent. A remarkable escape from the city noise.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Taxco (Silver City)
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Hillside colonial silver-mining town with cobblestone streets and a dramatic baroque cathedral. About 3 hours by bus from the city.

safety_tips: Mexico City is much safer than its historical reputation. Tourist areas (Polanco, Condesa, Roma, Coyoacán, Centro) are low-risk during the day
Use Uber or DiDi instead of hailing street taxis — registered apps are safer
Keep valuables in your hotel safe and carry a small amount of cash for street food and metro
Altitude (2,240m) affects many visitors — stay hydrated, avoid alcohol the first day, and rest if you feel dizzy
Learn a few words of Spanish — locals appreciate the effort enormously
Be careful with tap water — drink bottled or filtered water throughout your stay
